turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I'm here about Owen. I have until 4:40, so let's not waste it. Who decided to give him a zero, and did anyone speak to him before it went in the gradebook?
"I've heard your points." That isn't an answer, Hale. Tell me who entered the zero and whether anyone spoke to Owen first, or I'm writing down that you didn't.
With respect, this is exactly what lawyers do. Make noise until the facts go away.
Then put the facts on the table, Hale. So far I've heard one fact, that a zero is in the gradebook, and I'm the one who had to tell you Owen found out from his phone. What do you have?
Your son cheated, and you're teaching him that Mom can make it disappear.
My child never lies. You've called him a cheater without one document in your hand, and I'm writing that down. Show me something I can check, Hale, or I'm walking to the principal's office.
